title: 3Q2026 ING press release
body_markdown:
**3Q2026 net result of €1,850 million, up 3.5% year-on-year with an ROTE of 16.3%**


Mobile primary customer base increases by 259,000 in the third quarter


Net core lending growth of €11.0 billion and net core deposit growth of €12.1 billion


Fee income of €1,273 million, up 9.3% year-on-year


Operating expenses remain under control; risk costs affected by a management overlay


Profit before tax increases 5.7% year-on-year to €2,705 million


Strong capital generation and CET1 ratio of 13.3% allow us to announce a €1.9 billion distribution


We are refocusing and simplifying Wholesale Banking to better serve our clients


## CEO statement


“ING has had a strong third quarter of 2026 as we continue to execute on our strategy and deliver solid commercial and financial performance,” said Steven van Rijswijk, CEO of ING. “Against a backdrop of continuing geopolitical uncertainty, volatility and pressure on consumer and corporate confidence, our clients continue to show their trust in ING and increasingly turn to us for more of their financial needs across our various segments. This demonstrates the strength and resilience of our business, and we remain well on track to deliver on our outlook for 2026.


“We’re proud that more customers are choosing ING as their bank. We have added 259,000 mobile primary customers during the quarter, with strong contributions from Germany, the Netherlands and Romania. Total income has grown 5.6% and net result has increased 3.5% year-on-year. As our customer base grows, we are also doing more business with them and seeing higher customer balances, which contributed to double-digit growth in commercial interest income and 9.3% growth in fee income year-on-year. This was partly offset by lower other income, reflecting effects from heightened interest rate volatility, which are expected to reverse over time.


“In Retail Banking, our mortgage portfolio has increased by €6.9 billion as we helped more people finance their homes, contributing to lending growth of €8.5 billion, or up 6% annualised. Deposits have grown by €2.7 billion, despite seasonal customer summer holiday spending. As more customers choose to invest with ING, we have also seen continued flows from deposits into investment products, which supported a €6.7 billion increase in assets under management & e-brokerage during the quarter to €328 billion, up 22% year-on-year.


“In Wholesale Banking, lending growth was €2.5 billion on the back of continued client demand. Deposits have grown by €9.4 billion, highlighting good deposit-gathering momentum. Fee income has increased 9.4% year-on-year, with strong contributions from Daily Banking & Trade Finance. As part of the ambition to become the best European bank, we are taking a next strategic step in Wholesale Banking to simplify and make it easier for our clients to do business with us. As a reliable banking partner, we aim to create greater value for our clients and all our stakeholders.


“Operating expenses have remained under control, with a 1.1% increase quarter-on-quarter as higher staff expenses reflecting wage inflation were partly mitigated by the ongoing implementation of cost initiatives. Risk costs excluding one-offs remained well below our through-the-cycle average of 20 basis points of average customer lending. Return on tangible equity was 16.3% in the quarter, with a four-quarter-rolling-average of 14.8%.


"Our capital remains strong, with a CET1 ratio of 13.3%. In line with our capital velocity ambitions, we completed two significant risk-transfer (SRT) transactions during the quarter, generating total RWA relief of €3.0 billion. These included a transaction for Wholesale Banking and one for Retail Banking.


"Operating at the right level of capital is in the best interest of all our stakeholders, including our customers and the economies where we do business. After completing the share buyback programme that we announced in April 2026, we today announce a further distribution of €1.9 billion.


“We enter the remainder of this year with good momentum and continued customer growth. I would like to thank our employees for their dedication to supporting our customers and clients and for driving our progress in a complex geopolitical and macroeconomic environment. We remain focused on delivering our strategic priorities and look forward to providing an update on our strategy at our Capital Markets Day on 14 June 2027.”


More details in the[3Q2026 press release download](https://ing.com/binaries/content/assets/documents/results/3q2026/3q2026-ing-press-release.pdf) .

### **ING profile**


ING is a global financial institution with a strong European base, offering banking services through its operating company ING Bank. The purpose of ING Bank is: empowering people to stay a step ahead in life and in business. ING Bank’s more than 60,000 employees offer retail and wholesale banking services to customers in over 100 countries.


ING Group shares are listed on the exchanges of Amsterdam (INGA NA, INGA.AS), Brussels and on the New York Stock Exchange (ADRs: ING US, ING.N).


ING aims to put sustainability at the heart of what we do. Our policies and actions are assessed by independent research and ratings providers, which give updates on them annually. ING's ESG rating by MSCI has been upgraded from 'AA' to 'AAA' in October 2025. As of July 2026, in Sustainalytics’ view, ING’s management of ESG material risk is ‘Strong’ with an ESG risk rating of 16.7 (low risk).


ING Group shares are also included in major sustainability and ESG index products of leading providers. Here are some examples: Euronext, STOXX, Morningstar and FTSE Russell.
